- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 3-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) declines after negative sentiment — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overpredict downward moves — apply upward bias of 1–3% for next 5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 1–3% upward bias if recent 10-day avg is > 75% of 30-day avg.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0 → +0.5), model fails to anticipate — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
